Bodyweight Flyes

Bodyweight Flyes is an intermediate isolation exercise targeting the chest. It uses ez bar and is suitable for intermediate trainees.

Specialist movement. This is a sport-specific or conditioning drill that we keep for reference. It is not part of our main exercise library or planner. Looking for standard strength exercises? Browse the exercise library.

How To Perform

  1. 1 Position two equally loaded EZ bars on the ground next to each other. Ensure they are able to roll.
  2. 2 Assume a push-up position over the bars, supporting your weight on your toes and hands with your arms extended and body straight.
  3. 3 Place your hands on the bars. This will be your starting position.
  4. 4 Using a slow and controlled motion, move your hands away from the midline of your body, rolling the bars apart. Inhale during this portion of the motion.
  5. 5 After moving the bars as far apart as you can, return to the starting position by pulling them back together. Exhale as you perform this movement.

Form Cues

  • ✓ Focus on controlled movement throughout each rep.
  • ✓ Maintain proper alignment and avoid compensating with other muscle groups.
  • ✓ Breathe out during the exertion phase of the movement.

Common Mistakes

  • ✗ Using too much weight before mastering the technique.
  • ✗ Rushing through reps — prioritize control over speed.
  • ✗ Not achieving full range of motion on each repetition.
💡 Professor Splits Says:

Progressive overload is the engine of muscle growth. Track your weights and aim to add small increments weekly. For Bodyweight Flyes, this means gradually increasing load, volume (sets × reps), or decreasing rest periods over time.

FAQ

How many sets of Bodyweight Flyes should I do?▾
3 sets of 12–15 reps is a solid starting point. Adjust based on your training frequency and overall weekly volume for chest. Beginners should start with the lower end; advanced trainees can push toward the upper range.
What muscles does Bodyweight Flyes target?▾
Bodyweight Flyes primarily targets the Chest. Secondary muscles include Core, Shoulders, Triceps.
Is Bodyweight Flyes good for beginners?▾
Bodyweight Flyes is rated intermediate. Beginners should build foundational strength first with simpler movements.
How much rest between sets?▾
For Bodyweight Flyes, 60 sec of rest between sets is recommended. Isolation exercises can typically use shorter rest periods (45–90 sec) to maintain the pump and time efficiency.
